---
title: "R only vs R + T"
---

```{python}
from _lib import *
met = read("validation_metrics")
held = read("heldout")
```

Most field spectra are reflectance-only, while integrating-sphere data also have
transmittance. For leaves with both, the same model is fitted twice:

1. **Using R and T.** This gives the best use of the data; transmittance from integrating
   spheres can be noisy, and the error model gives it its own scale.
2. **Using R only, and then predicting T.** This is a structural, out-of-sample test of the
   RTM (objective A).

These fits also answer objective B's question: do trait estimates improve when T is used?

## Held-out transmittance

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "Prediction of measured transmittance from fits that used reflectance only: median per-leaf RMSE and bias, and the share of bands inside the 90 % prediction band of the RTM output."
if len(held):
    show_table(fmt(held.assign(run=lambda d: d.apply(run_label, axis=1))[["run", "quantity", "n", "rmse", "bias", "coverage90"]]))
else:
    no_data()
```

## Do traits improve with T?

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Log-CRPS (lower is better) of trait estimates from R-only vs R+T fits of the same leaves (leaves with both R and T), per RTM × error model × trait. Points below the 1:1 line: T helps."
duc = read("data_use_comparison")
if len(duc):
    fig = go.Figure()
    for err, g in duc.groupby("errmodel"):
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=g["crps_log_R"], y=g["crps_log_RT"], mode="markers+text",
                                 text=g["model"].map(MODEL_LABEL) + " " + g["trait"], textposition="top center",
                                 textfont=dict(color=INK2, size=10), name=ERR_LABEL.get(err, err),
                                 marker=dict(size=11, color=ERR_COLOR.get(err), line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=2))))
    v = np.r_[duc["crps_log_R"], duc["crps_log_RT"]]
    one_to_one(fig, np.nanmin(v), np.nanmax(v))
    fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="log-CRPS, R only", yaxis_title="log-CRPS, R + T", height=480,
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.1))
    show(fig)
    show_table(fmt(duc))
else:
    no_data()
```
